# 1 Clement Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_008_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 8 is almost entirely composed of scripture citations about repentance, anchoring the call to repentance in divine authority. The composite quotation in v.3 (combining elements of Ezekiel 33:11, Isaiah 1, and possibly a lost catechetical text) is one of the more puzzling textual issues in 1 Clement. The phrase "say 'Father'" has no exact parallel in the Hebrew/LXX tradition and may reflect early Christian prayer practice (*Abba* / *Pater*).

The Isaiah 1:16-20 citation (v.4) is close to the LXX, with minor variations. Clement uses the full prophetic sequence: cleanse → stop evil → do good → seek justice → help the vulnerable → the Lord's reasoning with us → conditional promise and threat.

Key translation debate: v.2 "I desire not the death of the sinner" (EMET) vs. "I take no pleasure in the death of the sinner" (LOGOS). The Greek *boulomai* = to will/desire/take pleasure in. SOPHIA preserves "I desire not" as more literal.

---

## Chapter 8

**8:1** The ministers of the grace of God spoke through the Holy Spirit concerning repentance.

**8:2** And even the Sovereign Lord of all things spoke of repentance with an oath: "As I live, says the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner but rather his repentance." And he added a gracious declaration: [Ezek 33:11]

**8:3** "Repent, O house of Israel, from your iniquity. Say to the sons of my people: Even though your sins reach from the earth to the heaven, and though they be redder than scarlet and blacker than sackcloth, if you turn to me with your whole heart and say 'Father,' I will hearken to you as to a holy people." [composite citation]

**8:4** And in another place he speaks thus: "Wash and be clean; put away your evil deeds from before my eyes; cease from your wickedness; learn to do good; seek justice; rescue the wronged; give judgment for the orphan, and defend the widow; and come, let us reason together, says the Lord; and if your sins be as crimson, I will make them white as snow; and if they be as scarlet, I will make them white as wool; and if you are willing and hear me, you shall eat the good things of the land; but if you are unwilling and do not hear me, a sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things." [Isa 1:16-20 LXX]

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
